title: Travelers Lose Nearly $2,500 to Trip Troubles
paragraphs: A fridge magnet is a nice thing to bring home from a holiday. A broken leg? Not so much!
But that's exactly what happened on the second day of a two-week trip to one respondent in a recent survey. And they were far from alone in having a holiday go wrong.

The survey by Talker Research of 4,000 travelers from the US, UK and Australia found that 73% had experienced a major travel problem. Respondents said that their travel problems had cost them nearly $2,500 on average.

Bad weather was the most common problem, affecting 26% of respondents. Another 16% had become sick or gotten hurt, while 14% had arrived at a hotel only to find that some facilities weren't available.
Another 14% had their phone die or their internet stop working when they needed it most. Getting lost was just as common, with 14% saying this had happened to them.
One traveler said their flight home was canceled at the last minute. Their partner had to drive six hours through the night to pick them up.
Because of these experiences, 85% said they now plan and book their trips differently.
Many travelers are also asking AI for help with their trips. Some 67% said they had used it to find travel information.
However, while 75% would trust AI to recommend a hotel, only 14% would trust it to book their stay on its own.
